market_question: Will Dan Cox win the 2026 Maryland Governor Republican primary election?
reasoning: Dan Cox won the 2022 primary but lost the general election by a 32-64% landslide, leaving many Maryland Republicans questioning his electability. The party is likely to nominate a more centrist candidate in 2026, possibly splitting the conservative vote. While early, I estimate Cox’s true probability at ~40%, below the market’s 57.5%.
evidence_points: Cox lost the 2022 general election to Wes Moore by over 30 points, a historic margin in Maryland.
Former governor Larry Hogan’s moderate wing remains influential and may back a more viable primary challenger.
No public polling yet, but historical patterns show parties tend to pivot after such defeats.
sources_consulted: Recall of Maryland 2022 gubernatorial primary and general election results
General knowledge of Maryland Republican dynamics and Larry Hogan’s role
